subject: Audit & access log exports — serialization, batch windows, and erase-proof guidance
messages:
From: Sara Li <sara.li@acmehealth.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
Cc: Legal Ops <legal-ops@acmehealth.com>
Date: Thu, 28 May 2026 17:14:00 -0700
Subject: Questions on audit/access log retention and export for legal hold

Hi Naomi,

Quick set of questions from our compliance team as we prepare a legal hold for a subset of accounts:

1) What is Redwood's default retention for hosted audit/access logs (admin events, auth events, read/write traces)?
2) Can we export a full historic slice (UTC time range) and get it in a single archive that preserves event ordering? We need an immutable proof-of-export for our records.
3) If we request a preservation window beyond the default retention (legal hold), can Redwood guarantee we won't see deletion? Are there environment restrictions (hosted vs. dedicated vs. private)?
4) What formats and metadata do exports include (checksums, sequence numbers, tombstone markers)?
5) Lead time and SLA for a 180-day slice for ~120M events — estimate of turnaround and cost ballpark would help.

Appreciate concise answers — legal ops wants this in writing to decide next steps.

Thanks,
Sara
Sara Li
Security & Privacy Lead, Acme Health
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Li <sara.li@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Legal Ops <legal-ops@acmehealth.com>
Date: Fri, 29 May 2026 09:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Questions on audit/access log retention and export for legal hold

Hi Sara — thanks for the clear list. Long answer short: yes, we can deliver what you describe, with some caveats depending on deployment type. Below is a concise runbook and what to expect.

1) Default retention (hosted): audit and access traces are retained for 90 days in the hosted control plane. Dedicated customers can configure longer retention (up to 365 days) via a retention flag on the reserved capacity contract. Private (VPC/on-prem) customers control retention entirely and can retain for any period per their policy.

2) Export slices and ordering: we export slices in NDJSON or compressed CSV. Each event record includes a monotonic sequence_id and ISO-8601 timestamp; exports are serialized in ascending sequence_id to preserve causal ordering. For very large exports we ship chunked archives (batch-serial-0001.tar.gz, batch-serial-0002.tar.gz) that represent contiguous sequence ranges; a top-level manifest lists the sequence ranges per chunk.

3) Legal hold / preservation windows: hosted tenants cannot opt-out of automated retention deletion beyond contractual add-ons — for a legal hold beyond default retention we need either (a) to be on Dedicated with retention extension enabled, or (b) to move to Private where you control retention. For hosted customers we offer a temporary export-and-archive service (we produce an evidence package and manifest, and you ingest to your archive) but we cannot indefinitely prevent deletion in the multi-tenant hosted environment. If you need Redwood to guarantee preservation on our side, Dedicated or Private is required.

4) Export metadata & proof: exports include: sequence_id, event_type, timestamp, tenant_id, object_id, actor_id, op_type, and a tombstone_flag for deletions. Each chunk has a SHA256 checksum and the manifest is signed by Redwood's export-key (we provide the public key). The evidence_manifest_sample.txt attached shows the fields and signature format.

5) Lead time & throughput estimate (180-day, ~120M events): typical throughput for a bulk export is ~15-50M events/day depending on time-range density; for your dataset we'd estimate 3–8 business days for export prep + run. We recommend a 72-hour minimum prep window for scheduling and throttling. Cost: rough ballpark for hosted export service is $Xk–$Yk depending on compression ratio and requested SLA (we'll provide a formal quote after we profile a sample).

Next steps: if you want Redwood to host the preserved copy under our control, let us know and we'll discuss Dedicated sizing. Otherwise we can begin the export and deliver the signed evidence package for you to archive.

Let me know which path you prefer and I'll loop in engineering for scheduling.

Best,
Naomi Feldman
Senior Security Solutions Manager | Redwood Inference

- Confirm export SLA & cost band for a 180-day / ~120M events export (prep + run + signed manifest). They asked for a ballpark; engineering should confirm realistic throughput and whether 72hrs prep is safe.
- Sales: if preservation on Redwood side is requested, confirm contract/ops path for Dedicated sizing and pricing.
- CS: if we do the export-only path, let's offer the evidence manifest and a recommended retention import checklist for their archive (we should include the sample manifest and checksum validation steps).

All — quick response for Naomi to send back to Acme (I will own the Dedicated pricing follow-up):

- Export SLA & timing: Engineering confirmed bulk export for their size (120M events) can be completed in 4 business days once scheduled. We should quote 6 business days to be conservative (2 days prep + 4 days run).
- Cost ballpark: for hosted export service we should propose $12,500–$18,000 depending on compression and whether they require archived storage with retrieval windows. I will refine if they ask for a firm quote.
- Preservation guarantee: for Redwood to guarantee retention on our side we need them on Dedicated (minimum 2-week procurement to configure retention flag) — pricing is separate. For legal holds on hosted we provide the signed export only.
- Deliverables: NDJSON chunked archives, top-level signed manifest with per-chunk SHA256, and a signed timestamped attestation file. Attachments we send: audit_export_schema_v2.ndjson (sample), evidence_manifest_sample.txt.

Naomi — send this back to Sara. I'll open a Dedicated commercial thread and loop in pricing. Marissa — can you draft the recommended ingest checklist (hash verification steps and sample S3 layout) and drop it in the Drive link Naomi referenced?

Thanks,
Ben
Head of Sales Engineering | Redwood Inference
